references.text: Kiriath-arba is mentioned as the original name of Hebron, where Sarah died and Abraham bought the burial site in the cave of Machpelah.
Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had lived as foreigners.
Explains that Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba, named after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim.
Hebron was designated as one of the cities of refuge in the hill country of Judah.
Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, was given to the clans of Caleb, but the city itself became a Levitical city.
Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron, formerly known as Kiriath-arba.
David was anointed king over Judah in Hebron, showing the city's importance as a major center.
The spies came to Hebron, where the Anakim Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai lived. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
